name: math_eval
description: Exact arithmetic and scalar functions: Decimal/Fraction/float modes, logs, roots, trig in rad and deg, hyperbolic, combinatorics, statistics and distributions, Italian finance (VAT, withholding, loans, NPV, IRR, DCF), unit conversion, CODATA physical constants via const("h").

name: math_solve
description: Symbolic math with SymPy plus SciPy/NumPy: equations, systems, inequalities, derivatives, integrals (single, multiple, line, surface), limits, series, function study, vector calculus, Lagrange, ODE, Laplace, Fourier/FFT, Riccati LQR, linear algebra, sums, recurrences, polynomials, complex numbers, thermodynamic potentials and Maxwell relations from U, H, A, G, S, Omega or an equation of state, quantum wavefunctions (probability density and current, probability of a region, momentum space, Schroedinger check), Lagrangian mechanics (Euler-Lagrange equations, generalized momenta, Hamiltonian and Hamilton's equations, action along a path), central-force orbits with the Binet equation (force law from an orbit, orbit from a force law), the first Born approximation of scattering by a central potential V(r) (amplitude and cross section in q or theta, a Coulomb tail regularized; numbers for any V(r), Woods-Saxon too, with at). Results are self-verified.

expr.description: Scalar expression, equation with '=', or ';'-separated equations/vector components.

variables.description: Variables of expr; for lagrangian the generalized coordinates, functions of t, with x' for dx/dt in expr (e.g. ["x", "theta"]).

bounds.description: [a, b] for integrate/summation, [point, dir] for limit, [x0] for series, [[x,a,b],[y,c,d],...] for multi_integrate/surface_integral, [t0, t1] for numeric ode, [t1, t2] for the action of lagrangian.

ics.description: Initial conditions for ODE e.g. {'y(0)': 1, "y'(0)": 0} or recurrence e.g. {'a(0)': 0, 'a(1)': 1}, or u = 1/r for central_force e.g. {'u(0)': 0.5, "u'(0)": 0}.

potential.description: For thermo_relations: what expr is. U(S, V), H(S, p), A(T, V), G(T, p), S(U, V, N), the grand potential Omega(T, V, mu), or eos = an equation of state p(V, T). N (amount) is optional in U, H, A, G and gives mu. Other names in expr are constants.

potential_energy.description: For born_scattering: the central potential V(r), r the distance, every other name a positive constant (q, k, theta, mu, hbar are names of the result), e.g. "-V0*exp(-r/a)/r"; a Coulomb tail L/r is regularized with exp(-epsilon*r). For lagrangian: V(q, q', t), with kinetic_energy (L = T - V). For wavefunction: V of the space variables (and t); gives result.schrodinger (energy of an eigenstate, or the residual of the time-dependent equation when expr has t).

momentum_space.description: For wavefunction: add the momentum-space wavefunction Phi(p_x, ...).

kinetic_energy.description: For lagrangian, instead of expr: the kinetic energy T(q, q', t), e.g. "m*(r'**2 + r**2*phi'**2)/2"; L = T - potential_energy.

path.description: For lagrangian: a path {coordinate: expression of t}, e.g. {"x": "A*cos(w*t)"}, with bounds [t1, t2]: gives result.action (S = integral of L dt and whether the path is stationary).

orbit.description: For central_force: the orbit r(theta), e.g. "p/(1 + e*cos(theta))"; gives the force law F(r). mu is the (reduced) mass, l the angular momentum, other names positive constants.

force.description: For central_force: the force F(r), negative = attractive, e.g. "-k/r**2"; gives the orbit r(theta) from the Binet equation u'' + u = -mu F/(l^2 u^2), u = 1/r, when it is linear in u.

at.description: For thermo_relations: numbers for the symbols, e.g. {"T": 300, "V": 0.0224, "n": 1, "R": 8.314462618}; adds result.values. For born_scattering: numbers > 0 for every constant of V, mu, hbar and q (or k and theta in radians), e.g. {"V0": 50, "a": 1.2, "mu": 1, "hbar": 1, "q": 0.8}: gives result.values (q, f, dsigma_dOmega) from the numerical integral, without the closed form.

coords.description: Coordinate system for multi_integrate (Jacobian added automatically).

domain.description: Domain of the unknowns for solve; for lagrangian the constants are real (default) or positive (masses, lengths, c: simpler square roots).

numeric_samples.description: Signal array for fourier_fft, initial guess for optimize_num.

name: number_theory
description: Integer and modular arithmetic with exact big integers: primality, factorization, divisors, totient, Mobius, primes, gcd/lcm/extended gcd, modular power/inverse/square root/log, primitive roots, Legendre/Jacobi, CRT, Diophantine equations, continued fractions, partitions, digits.

n.description: Main integer (decimal string allowed for big numbers).

values.description: Integers for gcd/lcm, residues for crt.

expr.description: Equation for diophantine; number for continued_fraction (e.g. 'sqrt(7)', '415/93').

name: math_numeric
description: Numerical math with mpmath, SciPy and NumPy: arbitrary precision evaluation (up to 1000 digits), infinite sums, numerical integrals, roots, constrained and global optimization, linear and integer programming, ODE initial value problems with events (stop when an expression reaches zero), polynomial roots, closed-form identification of constants, curve fitting.

expr.description: Expression, equation with '=', ';'-separated equations, or ';'-separated ODE right-hand sides.

bounds.description: [a, b] or [[x,a,b],...] for quad/nsum, [lo, hi] bracket for root, [[lo, hi], ...] per variable for minimize/linprog, [t0, t1] for ode_ivp.

x0.description: Initial guess, or initial state for ode_ivp.

events.description: ode_ivp only: zero crossings of expressions in the variables. A terminal event stops the integration; a zero exactly at t0 does not count. Example: [{"expr": "y", "direction": "falling"}] stops when y comes down to 0.

name: math_verify
description: Check an answer before giving it: symbolic and random-point equivalence of two expressions, substitution of a solution into equations, derivative and antiderivative checks, numeric comparison with tolerance, counterexample search for inequalities, dimensional check of a formula with units (check_units).

expr.description: Expression, ';'-separated equations, or inequality to check.

expected.description: Claimed result to compare with; for check_units the expected unit of the expression, e.g. "N".

solution.description: Claimed solution: values e.g. {'x': '2', 'y': '-1/3'}, or functions for a differential equation written with diff(), e.g. {'y': 'exp(x)'} for diff(y, x) - y = 0.

units.description: check_units: unit of each variable, e.g. {"F": "N", "rho": "kg/m^3", "v": "m/s", "Cd": "1"}; SI prefixes allowed (kN, MPa, mA); degC for Celsius, "C" is the coulomb.

name: python_sandbox
description: Run a short Python program in a restricted interpreter for problems no other tool covers (counting, brute force, sequences, multi-step computations). Allowed imports: math, cmath, fractions, decimal, itertools, functools, collections, statistics, random, heapq, bisect, sympy, numpy, scipy, mpmath. No files, no network, 5 s limit. Returns printed output and the value of the last expression.

code.description: Python source, max 8000 characters. Use print() or end with an expression.

name: lean_check
description: Check a formal proof in Lean 4 with Mathlib. Returns whether it compiles without errors, without sorry and with only the standard axioms, with Lean messages. Code that runs programs (#eval, run_cmd, elab, macro), new axioms and native_decide are rejected. 60 s limit.

code.description: Lean 4 source, max 20000 characters. 'import Mathlib' is added if no import is present.

name: date_calc
description: Dates and times in the Italian calendar (Europe/Rome): exact age (also in months and weeks), weekday, differences (days, business days, real elapsed hours across DST) and additions, relative dates, events with DST offsets and reminders, recurring events, time zone conversion, invoice due dates (DFFM), month calendar, Italian national holidays including Easter and Easter Monday.

to_timezone.description: Target IANA zone for convert_tz, e.g. 'America/New_York'.

month_week.description: recurring monthly by weekday: 1 = first, -1 = last target_weekday of the month.

name: geom3d_calc
description: 3D geometry for CAD, CNC and robotics: vector operations, angles, rotations (Euler, axis-angle), 4x4 homogeneous transforms, quaternions, Denavit-Hartenberg forward kinematics, distances and intersections, cylindrical and spherical coordinates, bolt holes, solid and cross-section properties. For 3D drawing: 2D sketch profiles, circles through 3 points, fillets, triangle solving, curves as point lists (helix, involute, spline, parametric), CAD pick points on faces and edges, patterns, point clouds, mesh and composite part checks (volume, centroid, bounding box).

dh_table.description: List of [a, alpha_deg, d, theta_deg] rows for dh_kinematics.

name: eng_calc
description: Engineering design formulas: strength of materials (Hooke, beams, shafts, Von Mises/Tresca, Euler buckling, fatigue, pressure vessels, bolts, welds), machine design (dynamics, vibrations, gears, bearings L10, belts, CNC cutting), fluids and heat (pipes, drag/lift, heat transfer, heatsinks), electrical and control (AC/DC, RLC filters, Clarke/Park, second-order systems, PID, optics, acoustics), material properties; hydrostatics, pumps and hydraulic cylinders, open channels (Manning), flow meters and weirs, compressible flow (isentropic, normal shock, choked), ideal gas states and processes, thermodynamic cycles (Carnot, Otto, Diesel, Brayton), calorimetry; thermal stresses, Hertz contact, helical compression springs, interference (press and shrink) fits, strain transformation and strain-gauge rosettes; CODATA physical constants; chemistry (molar mass from a formula, balancing and stoichiometry, pH of strong and weak acids and bases and buffers, dilution and molarity, Arrhenius and integrated rate laws, Nernst, Faraday electrolysis, Gibbs energy and K); nuclear physics (AME2020/NUBASE2020 nuclide data: masses, binding energy, half-lives, decay modes; radioactive decay law, activity, parent-daughter chains; reaction and decay Q-values with conservation checks and thresholds); modern physics (photon, photoelectric effect, Compton, relativistic de Broglie wavelength, hydrogen-like atoms, blackbody, uncertainty principle); special relativity (gamma, energy and momentum, time dilation, length contraction, velocity addition, Doppler, Lorentz transformation, mass-energy); water and steam with IAPWS-IF97 (state from (p,T), (p,x), (T,x), (p,h), (p,s), (p,v), (T,v); saturation tables; Rankine cycle with pump and turbine efficiencies and reheat); psychrometrics of moist air (state from dry bulb and relative humidity, humidity ratio, wet bulb, dew point or enthalpy; mixing of two streams; heating and cooling coils with condensate; evaporative cooling); convection heat transfer coefficients from Nusselt correlations (laminar flat plate, cylinder in crossflow, sphere, pipe flow laminar and turbulent with Gnielinski, Dittus-Boelter, Sieder-Tate; natural convection on vertical and horizontal plates, horizontal cylinders, spheres and horizontal enclosures); heat exchangers with the effectiveness-NTU method (parallel, counter, crossflow mixed and unmixed, phase change; rating and sizing); straight fins of uniform cross-section with the four tip conditions, fin efficiency and overall efficiency of fin arrays; lumped-capacitance transient with the Biot number check); radiation exchange between gray diffuse surfaces (2D view factors, two-surface enclosures and parallel plates with radiation shields, N-surface enclosures with the radiosity method); electrostatics (Coulomb's law, field, potential and energy of point charges, capacitance of parallel plates, coaxial and eccentric cylinders, parallel wires, wire near a wall, concentric spheres, isolated sphere and disc, capacitor combinations); magnetism (field of a straight wire, loop, finite and long solenoid, toroid; force between parallel wires and on a wire; Lorentz force and cyclotron motion); inductance of solenoids, toroids, coaxial cables, straight wires, loops, rectangles, wire pairs and Wheeler coils; electromagnetic induction (Faraday flux change, rotating coil, moving rod); linkages (Grashof condition and the eight-case classification of four-bar linkages, four-bar position and velocity, slider-crank piston motion, quick-return time ratio) and planetary gear trains (Willis relation, planet speed, differential); catenary cables (from span and length with level or unequal supports, from sag, from horizontal tension) and journal bearings (Sommerfeld number, Petroff friction torque and power loss); pin-jointed 2D and 3D trusses with the direct stiffness method (member forces and stresses, reactions, nodal displacements, strain energy, degree of static indeterminacy); torsion of non-circular sections (circle, annulus, ellipse, equilateral triangle, rectangle by Fourier series, thin-walled open and closed sections by Bredt: torsion constant, maximum shear stress, twist angle); geometric optics (thick lenses, mirrors, refracting surfaces, lens pairs) and wave optics (Malus, Brewster, Fresnel, slits, gratings, thin films, Rayleigh); practical electronics (LED resistor, op-amp circuits, Wheatstone bridge, 555 timer, thermistors); friction in simple machines (inclined plane, leadscrew, rolling resistance); electric machines (transformer, DC, induction and synchronous motors); thin circular and rectangular plates; continuous beams (three moments); local losses at sudden changes of section (Borda-Carnot); stress concentration at holes (Kirsch, Inglis); rotor balancing (one and two planes, ISO grades); rolling without slipping; kinetic theory of gases (molecular speeds, Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution, kinetic pressure, mean free path and collision frequency, wall flux and effusion, Graham's law, equipartition and heat capacities); Newtonian gravitation (two bodies, field and potential of point masses, uniform sphere and hollow shell with the binding energy, ring on its axis, effective gravity on a rotating body, Gauss's law, potential difference and the uniform-field approximation); statistical mechanics (Gibbs and Boltzmann entropy, entropy from heat and entropy generated, relativistic Maxwell-Juttner gas, translational, vibrational and rotational partition functions with U, S, A and C_V); waves (AM, FM and PM modulation indices, damped waves, superposition of plane waves, standing waves with nodes, beats with phase and group velocity, two waves out of phase, KdV soliton), reference_frames (Galilean frames r', v', a' and the apparent force, rotation about a fixed axis, rotating frames: rate of a vector, Coriolis, centrifugal and Euler accelerations; Euler's equations of a rigid body with the inertia tensor), nuclear_scattering (Breit-Wigner resonance cross section with the statistical factor and the lifetime, Rutherford cross section with impact parameter, turning point and counts from the fluence, Mott cross section of two identical particles of spin s), em_radiation (Poynting vector and its flux through a flat surface, plane-wave fields, intensity, energy and momentum density, radiation pressure with reflectance and angle), photometry (luminosity distance, apparent and absolute magnitudes, distance modulus, colour indices U - B and B - V, bolometric correction).

params.description: Operation-specific SI/engineering inputs (all keys explicitly documented & Pydantic-validated).
